hints: Focus on using standard enthalpies of formation with Hess's law, where reaction enthalpy equals products minus reactants.
Remember that elements in their standard states like N2(g) and O2(g) have zero enthalpy of formation, so decomposing N2O must give a large negative value.
Write balanced equations for each statement and calculate the sign of delta H to check if heat is released, then see which combination fits.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Hess's law rule**

Think of enthalpy of formation as the energy cost to make a compound from its elements. To find any reaction enthalpy, use products minus reactants.

$$\Delta H_r^\ominus = \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{reactants})$$

**Check statement 1: oxidation of N2O**

First balance the equation. One mole of N2O needs to make two moles of NO2.

$$\text{N}_2\text{O(g)} + \tfrac{3}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2\text{(g)}$$ 
Now calculate: $\Delta H = 2(+33) - [(+82) + 0] = 66 - 82 = -16 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. The negative sign means 16 kJ is released. So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2: decomposition of N2O**

Write the decomposition to elements in standard states.

$$\text{N}_2\text{O(g)} \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{(g)} + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$$ 
Calculate: $\Delta H = [0 + 0] - (+82) = -82 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. This is strongly exothermic because you are breaking down an endothermic compound. So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3: NO plus oxygen**

Balance the formation of NO2 from NO.

$$2\text{NO(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2\text{(g)}$$ 
Calculate: $\Delta H = 2(+33) - [2(+90) + 0] = 66 - 180 = -114 \text{ kJ}$. This is negative, so exothermic. So statement 3 is correct.

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all correct, the correct combination is selected.

options.A: Correct because all three statements are true. Statement 1 gives -16 kJ per mole of N2O, statement 2 gives -82 kJ, and statement 3 gives -114 kJ for 2 moles of NO. All are exothermic as claimed.
options.B: Incorrect because it omits one of the true statements. Students choose this if they make a balancing or arithmetic error, often on statement 1 where the 2 moles of NO2 are forgotten, giving +33 - 82 = -49 kJ instead of -16 kJ.
options.C: Incorrect because it omits one of the true statements. Students choose this if they doubt statement 1 because they are unsure how to balance N2O to NO2, or think oxygen has a non-zero enthalpy of formation.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only one or two statements. Students choose this if they think positive enthalpies of formation must mean all reactions are endothermic, forgetting that going from a more endothermic reactant to a less endothermic product releases heat.
